title: From empathy to digital attunement: rethinking syntony as a professional competence for teaching the Digital Generation
abstract: The dynamic digitisation of young people's lives is profoundly transforming education. The current generation students operates in an environment that is constantly mediated by technology, which is changing the way they communicate, build relationships and regulate their emotions. As a result, traditional approaches to empathy and ethical teaching concerns are proving insufficient in the face of new forms of presence, expression and interaction characteristic of young screen users. The article proposes a conceptual shift from empathy in the classical sense towards 'digital attunement', an expanded form of attunement that encompasses both emotional sensitivity and communication and regulatory skills appropriate to virtual environments. Using the results of research on teacher empathy, social-emotional competences and virtual empathy, an original four-dimensional model of teacher syntony in digital conditions was presented: perceptual syntony (recognition of emotional signals in the online space), emotional (co-regulation in screen situations), interactive (tuning digital communication, including modulation of tone, pace and form of communication) and reflective (awareness of one's o

title: Intrafamily relationships and depression as mediators of problematic Internet use among adolescents during remote learning in Poland
abstract: Estimating the extent to which (1) Pandemic Difficulties (PD) directly affects Internet Addiction (IA), and (2) the PD effect is mediated by Family Relationship (FR) and Children’s Depression (CD) of the test adolescents. 509 primary school students (11–16 years old) participated in a cross-sectional study. PD had a significant direct and positive effect on IA (β = .196). PD interacts with IA through FR and PD interacts with IA through FR and CD. Contrary to the direct effect, both were negative due to negative relationships between FR and IA (β = -.165) and between FR and CD (β = -.568). FR turned out to be a stronger mediator of the PD effect compared to CD. The difficulties of the epidemic have a significant impact on the increase in Internet addiction. The increase in depression caused by the epidemic’s difficulties may, in turn, lead to an increase in Internet addiction, while supportive family relationships play a protective role in this system.

title: Knowledge at the margins. Postdigital practices and educational authority in the classroom
abstract: This article challenges deficit-oriented narratives that portray adolescents’ engagement with digital media as risk or decline. Drawing on a two-year ethnographic study in Polish upper-secondary schools, it analyses how young people negotiate visibility in postdigital educational environments. Integrating perspectives from Hannah Arendt, Jacques Rancière and Shoshana Zuboff, the article conceptualises adolescent agency at the intersection of action, recognition, affect and algorithmic governance. Rather than off-task behaviour, students’ digital practices appear as attempts to become subjects of knowledge. The findings suggest that the so-called “e-generation crisis” reflects a misalignment between educational frameworks and postdigital conditions of learning. The study is based on two upper-secondary school classes and does not claim systemic representativeness; its aim is to identify and interpret recurring mechanisms and tensions rather than to generalise across the educational system.

title: The E-Crisis of Values among Teenagers as a Challenge for Contemporary Moral Education
abstract: Contemporary teenagers are growing up in a world of dynamic development of digital technologies, which influence the formation of their value system and moral attitudes. This article attempts to describe the phenomenon of the e-crisis of values. It manifests itself, among other things, in the relativisation of moral norms, the superficialisation of interpersonal relationships, dependence on opinions in social media, and difficulty in distinguishing between good and evil. This situation hinders the development of an integral moral identity in young people. The enormous prevalence of the internet, functioning in an instant culture, and the pressure of digital self-presentation disrupt the process of moral maturation and weaken authentic contact with oneself and with other people. The article will also discuss the key challenges facing contemporary moral education. A new approach to axiological education that takes into account the realities of the digital world is of great importance. Greater involvement of teachers, parents and educators as guides in shaping the moral identity of young people also plays an important role. The main objective of the article is to highlight the problem

title: New Anthropological Sensitivities and the Attitudes of Polish Catholic Priests Toward Youth Suicide
abstract: In the face of the growing number of youth suicides, anthropology is opening up new research approaches: more empathetic, dialogical, and focused on individual subjectivity and suffering. The aim of this article is to frame the topic of youth suicide within the perspective of sensitive anthropology and present selected results of fieldwork conducted in 2024 and 2025. This research attempts to identify contemporary attitudes of Polish Catholic clergy towards the phenomenon of suicide in the context of doctrinal and social changes. To achieve the research objectives, qualitative research methods were employed – a case study of the phenomenon, including a review of the relevant literature and content analysis of in-depth interviews conducted with 30 clergy, varying in age and place of ministry. They revealed diverse experiences and willingness to support those in crisis, reflected on funeral practices, the role of religion in prevention, and the perception of the Church as responding, or not, to the new existential challenges of youth. This new anthropological approach assumes a shift from moralizing judgment to listening, accompaniment, and understanding. Working within an interpreti

title: Beyond the e-crisis narrative: e-intensification of peer relations and the social mechanisms of bullying
abstract: In public debate, a narrative of an “e-crisis” of the younger generation has increasingly emerged, in which digital technologies are portrayed as the primary cause of adolescents’ deteriorating psychosocial functioning. This article offers a critical reflection on this diagnosis and proposes the conceptual framework of e-intensification as an analytical tool for reinterpreting the mechanisms of peer violence in adolescence. Rather than adopting an offline–online dichotomy, the framework focuses on changes in relational conditions, such as increased visibility of interactions, accelerated feedback, diffusion of the bystander role, and the heightened reputational stakes of peer interactions. The article demonstrates that digital technologies do not create new mechanisms of peer violence but intensify existing group processes related to the regulation of status and belonging. The analysis leads to conclusions relevant for educational and preventive practice, highlighting the importance of addressing group norms and the role of bystanders.

title: The pressure of passion and the perception of one’s own passion in university students
abstract: This article considers the analysis of the level of passion pressure and its perception in three dimensions: personal benefits, the way it is acquired and the current degree of its balance with other everyday activities among Polish students. Moreover, the moderating role of flourishing in explaining the relationship between the analyzed variables was verified, taking into account the context - students' passions related to artistic activity. Research has shown that the relationship between the analyzed variables is not direct. Positive relationship between the passion pressure and the perception of personal benefits of passion were established. Engagement in a passionate activity was an important mediator of the relationship between passion pressure and personal benefits of passion and balancing passion.

title: The business model of higher education institutions and equal access to education: A comparative perspective between the USA and Poland
abstract: The article analyses the impact of higher education business models on equal access to education in the United States and Poland. The authors highlight that the growing dependence on market principles in higher education, as encapsulated by Clark's concept of the entrepreneurial university, has a significant impact on the operations of academic institutions, their financing structures, and their interactions with the broader social and economic environment. While this model does promote autonomy and innovation in the United States, it also leads to deepening social inequalities, high education costs, and a decline in public trust in educational institutions. In Poland, despite free full-time education being guaranteed in the constitution, there is a growing pressure to commercialise and diversify income sources, which also affects the system's selectivity. The article presents social trust as an important indicator of educational equality and justice, while highlighting the need to balance efficiency with the social mission of universities. While the entrepreneurial model offers opportunities for development, without mechanisms to control and protect academic values, it may transfo

title: “We really got fired up!”: Performing childhood by adults while playing bottle caps. A forest and playground pedagogy perspective
abstract: The starting point of this article is a question: what happens to adults when they engage in practices from their own childhood? The analysis focuses on the affective–bodily–verbal reactions of participants in a field-based gamified activity, which together form the phenomenon of performing childhood—identified in the research and defined in the article. The study was conducted in a Forest Pedagogical Settlement, a space dedicated to nature education as well as practices of mindfulness and contemplation. Within the trees, a bottle-cap race track was constructed, designed to stimulate attentiveness and cognitive sensitivity in both children and adults. This practice, however, revealed a phenomenon unexpected from the perspective of nature-based education: when adults drew upon their biographical memories of playground games, they entered reconstructions of childhood habitus. They displayed loud, competitive, risk-taking, or ostentatiously joyful behaviors—contrasting sharply with the contemplative character of the forest setting. To capture the dynamics of these processes, the article employs Erving Goffman’s dramaturgical theory of interaction, Victor Turner’s anthropology of perfo

title: „The manipulator in the mask of a victim?” An analysis of the psychosocial functioning of Jamie Miller’s fictional protagonist according to the I-Level Classification
abstract: This article presents a case study of the fictional character Jamie Miller from the third episode of the TV series Adolescence (2025, Netflix), analysed using the I-Level Classification (ILC) system. which is used to diagnose the level of interpersonal maturity. The analysis is based on Jamie's conversation with a forensic psychologist and indicates that he functions at the third level of the ILC, specifically within the manipulator (pragmatist) subtype. The article also attempts to place the analysis in a broader cultural context and considers the educational and diagnostic value of analysing fictional narratives. The article concludes with a reflection on the influence of contemporary cultural patterns - including toxic masculinity - on the formation of immature and defensive interpersonal attitudes in adolescents.

title: Physical activity and the well-being of young people in the digital age
abstract: The development of digital technologies has significantly transformed the everyday practices of young people, fostering a sedentary lifestyle and reducing levels of physical activity. These phenomena are increasingly interpreted as manifestations of a sedentary lifestyle crisis , which may have adverse consequences for both physical and mental health. The aim of the study was to assess the current and expected well-being of young women and men in Poland aged 16–25, as well as to analyze the relationship between well-being and the level of physical activity in the context of a health-promoting lifestyle in the digital age. In particular, the study sought to determine whether meeting the World Health Organization’s recommendations for physical activity is associated with higher levels of well-being, and whether well-being assessments vary according to selected sociodemographic factors and experiences related to sports participation. Data were collected from a representative random–quota sample (by age, gender, education, region, size of place of residence, and occupational status) of adult residents of Poland (n = 1,042). Inclusion criteria comprised permanent residence in Poland and

title: From screen time to mechanisms: Digital media risks and supports in adolescents with autism spectrum disorders (ASD)
abstract: "Screen time" debates often imply that more digital media use inevitably harms adolescent well-being, yet evidence syntheses typically show small and heterogeneous links for total time. Clearer associations emerge for mechanism-proximal risks: cyberharm (including cybervictimization), problematic/compulsive engagement with impaired control, and sleep-disrupting late-night use. Focusing on adolescents with autism spectrum disorders (ASD), we propose the F-A-V-S framework (Function–Activity– Vulnerability–Skill transfer) to explain why the same digital ecosystem can act as both scaffold and risk amplifier. We translate F-A-V-S into Mechanism-Targeted Media Management (MTM), a practical toolkit that prioritizes three intervention targets—sleep protection, cyberharm prevention/response, and impaired control—evaluated via proximal functional indicators rather than global reductions in screen time.

title: From e-crisis to e-happiness: The triad of digital technologies in IB Music as a model for Polish music education
abstract: This article examines how digital technologies are used in the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme Music course, focusing on the shift from passive consumption of technology (which we call e-crisis) towards its use as a tool of creative activity and reflective learning (e-happiness). A qualitative study based on the analysis of 10 YouTube recordings (5 Higher Level, 5 Standard Level) verifies the hypothesis that structural requirements for creative process documentation and reflection (Contemporary Music-Making) generate the complete triad of technology functions: T1 (medium of creativity), T2 (process documentation), T3 (presentation). The analysis reveals consistent patterns: HL recordings tend to exhibit the complete triad alongside marked reflectivity, while SL recordings focus primarily on T3. The article identifies implications for Polish music education, proposing adaptation of IB Music elements (music journal, portfolio assessment, technology triad) as mechanisms supporting the development of agency and digital competencies in the young generation.

title: Existential predictors of resilience among university students
abstract: The aim of the study was to determine the significance of indicators of the dimensions of existence (biological, psychological and noetic) in explaining students’ resilience, measured using the Resilience Assessment Questionnaire (QuR-26). The survey involved 271 participants, with a mean age of 22.17 years (SD=3.80). The regression analysis included indicators such as sense of meaning in life, life satisfaction, generalized self-efficacy, perseverance, problem-solving readiness, and personality dimensions according to the Big Five model. The analysis of the results showed that statistically significant predictors of resilience were life satisfaction, extraversion, sense of purpose in life, and self-efficacy. These findings may serve as a guideline for the development of preventive programs targeting secondary school students, as well as university students.

title: Teaching planning genres in Argentine university teacher education: Analysis of inclusion in curricula
abstract: Teaching planning involves a set of procedures and practices through which pedagogical intentions are articulated and enacted. In these processes, teaching planning genres (TPGs)—such as lesson plans, teaching sequences, curriculum designs, and course syllabi—play a central role. Despite their importance for didactics and teacher education, little research has examined how these genres are taught, read, and written in university teacher-training programs. This article reports on the documentary component of a mixed-methods study and analyzes the inclusion of TPGs in 66 pedagogical training course syllabi from an Argentine public university. Using a combination of corpus analysis and descriptive statistics, the study identifies the types of TPGs most frequently incorporated—lesson plans (76%), provincial curriculum designs (55%), teaching sequences (30%), and study plans (9%)—and characterizes three modalities of inclusion across courses: no inclusion, peripheral inclusion, and central inclusion. The findings show that pedagogical training subjects tend to integrate TPGs more systematically than disciplinary subjects, revealing institutional and curricular patterns that shape how fu

title: Review: Janusz Mariański, Religious Experience in Sociological Narrative. A Theoretical and Empirical Study,Adam Marszałek Publishing House, Toruń 2025, pp. 265
abstract: This text is a review of Janusz Mariański's book Religious Experience in Sociological Narrative. A Theoretical and Empirical Study published by Adam Marszałek Publishing House in Toruń. Reading this book provokes a look at religious experience as something that can be somehow noticeable, also for a sociological approach. The review provides both a comprehensive presentation of the monograph from a substantive perspective and a partially polemical analysis of more specific topics. The Author also shares with the reader his personal experience of the phenomenon of religious experience, which can serve as a practical and living example of the research being conducted by the Polish sociologist of religion in his new book.Keywords: religion, religious experience, sociology, meaning of life, faith.

title: Education in the service of deceleration - a pathway to saving humanity?
abstract: The purpose of this article is to present an argument for "education in the service of deceleration". The author's narrative begins with humanity as a phenomenon we must/should preserve in a world dominated by technology. Education is a momentous and responsible task, intended to help individuals continually develop to their full potential. Exploring diverse trails from the broadly defined humanities and social sciences, the author presents her arguments and contrasts two educational modalities, which she terms "education in the service of acceleration" and "education in the service of deceleration." The former shapes, the so-called "surfers," permanently riding the wave of civilisation, while the latter shapes, so-called "visionaries," who are/should be permanently ready to attest to their humanity. A creatively exploited trail, intended as an "instrument" for decelerating this acceleration, is H. Rosa's concept of resonance.

title: Courage in the sphere of educational alternatives. The testimony of Krystyna Starczewska
abstract: The aim of the article is to present courage as a pedagogical category, constituting an essential element in the pursuit and implementation of alternative educational pathways. It attempts to show courage both as a virtue and as a skill, analyzed from philosophical, psychological, and pedagogical perspectives. In this approach, courage is understood not only as an individual disposition but also as a capacity that can be developed and cultivated through the educational process.On this background, the article presents the figure of Krystyna Starczewska, a leader of non-public education in Poland after 1989. Particular attention is given to moments in her biography in which courage played a crucial role, guiding her toward new and unconventional educational solutions. The analysis encompasses both her personal and professional experiences, illustrating how courage became the foundation of her efforts to create an open, democratic, and free school.The primary source material consists of an original interview conducted with Krystyna Starczewska in February 2024, as well as her unpublished diary Długa Wędrówka. This document, covering Starczewska’s life from childhood to her involvement

title: Pre-service Teacher education in the context of the competence framework: an analysis of student teachers’ perceptions of professional competences
abstract: The objective of this study is to examine how second-year master’s student teachers self-assess selected professional competences defined in the Competence Framework for Graduates of Teacher Education (MŠMT, 2025) after completing the course School Didactics – Curriculum and before entering continuous teaching practice. The study focuses on subject-matter understanding, didactic content delivery, lesson planning, goal setting and assessment of learning. In a cross-sectional survey, we used a short self-reflection tool mapped to selected competence descriptors of the framework. The results show high confidence in lesson planning and formulating learning outcomes, but lower confidence in criterion-referenced formative assessment. These findings confirm the framework’s value as a tool for aligning curricula with expected outcomes and for supporting targeted self-reflection by student teachers.

title: Shaping skills as an important goal of modern upbringing
abstract: The article draws attention to the importance of skills in the changing labour market. An approach was proposed in which skills are not an alternative to knowledge, but together with it form the basis of competences. This convention discusses algorithmic and heuristic skills, hard and soft, and basic and transversal skills. The need to shape various skills in the family – as part of upbringing through work – was also pointed out.

title: Jan Patočka’s philosophy of education in the light of selected problems of his philosophical thought - the contexts and premises of explicating the meaning of education
abstract: The aim of this article is to present the specific features of Jan Patočka's philosophy of education in light of selected issues of his philosophical thought. Accordingly, education enables the realization of human development potential, while also introducing individuals to the path of self-education.Therefore, education is a response to the meaning and goal of human existence. The objective of education is to change the naive figures of human beings into beings striving to understand themselves and the world around them. This aim requires human openness and the pursuit of truth. In Jan Patočki’s view, education eliminates all “deficits” by forming the “inner person”. The model of educated people is closely related to the realization of the ideal of one’s humanity. For this reason, education must not be considered in an opportunistic manner as mere instrumental means reduced to the realization of “socio-utilitarian” aims.

title: The culture of silence at polish universities. Analysis of “blank sheets” in the context of the commons and organizational culture
abstract: The article discusses the culture of Polish universities. Interestingly, the lack of data from our inquiry has become a basis of the analysis. We refer to the shortage of data as “blank sheets” and we consider what “blank sheets” can tell us. The analysis has been carried out in the context of the commons theory. The research shows that the university is not an institution of the commons, which is understood not only as a resource but also as a form of relationship. The article starts with the description of the research, findings of which are then analyzed from the point of view of the commons understood in a broader sense than just natural or artificial resources. Finally, we ponder on how critical pedagogy and qualitative research may contribute to the “recovery” of the commons, or in other words the university.

title: The student at the centre: an alternative perception of the learner in the educational process on the example of personalized education
abstract: The aim of the considerations presented in this paper is to construct a characterization of student functioning in a school implementing the assumptions of personalized education. This concept is perceived as an approach to the school as a learning environment that exhibits certain features of alternativeness. The discussion first focuses on the students’ position within the school community and their relationships with other members of that community. Subsequently, reflection is directed toward describing selected components of the educational process as experienced and co-constructed by students understood as active and agentic subjects of their own learning. The considerations are based on a problem-oriented analysis of the relevant academic literature. The discussion allows for the conclusion that personalized education contributes not only to students’ educational success but may also constitute a formative experience. Participation in personalized education provides opportunities both for acquiring lifelong learning competencies and for being part of a community and supporting various aspects of other individuals’ development. It may therefore be regarded as an important fact

title: An introduction to punk pedagogy: teaching about punk, punk theorizing, and punk as a form of public pedagogy
abstract: This article examines the concept of punk pedagogy as an alternative way of thinking about education and science. To determine the specificity of this concept, the authors begin their inquiry by defining the notion of “punk” and sketching a theoretical framework for punk through philosophical lenses. Then they analyse three possible perspectives on punk pedagogy: teaching about punk, punk theorizing, and punk as a form of public pedagogy. Finally, they focus on the critique and defense of the concept of punk pedagogy. The authors argue that punk pedagogy is one of the possible responses to the social and educational crises that manifest in dehumanization, alienation, silencing, and the production of superfluous beings, both human and non-human.

title: 13 Reasons Why: The series as an alternative space of thanatoeducation
abstract: The article addresses the thanatoeducational potential of the series 13 Reasons Why (Netflix), analyzed as an example of an alternative educational space. The study is situated within the interpretive paradigm and employs hermeneutic content analysis of the first season. The analysis focuses on representations of death and dying, dimensions of corporeality, sociality, existentiality, spirituality, and symbolism, as well as depictions of grief and life in the perspective of death. The series emerges as a “teacher of the viewer,” provoking reflection on responsibility, relationality, and co-responsibility in social life. The author also highlights reception-related risks (including the Werther effect), emphasizing the necessity of pedagogical reflection and critical analysis of representations of death in popular culture. The article offers recommendations for educational practice, including communicative, (digital) media, and intervention-oriented education, as well as the development of sustainable support procedures in crisis situations.

title: Montessori teachers’ success and their professional role. A perspective of an alternative educational model
abstract: Maria Montessori developed an educational philosophy centered on supporting the child’s development through the creation of a prepared environment that respects the child’s innate desire to learn. The teacher acts as a facilitator and a guide, ready to reflect on and adapt their attitudes in response to the observed needs of the children, entailing a necessary personal transformation. The Montessori teacher’s role involves navigating numerous tensions, particularly in relation to traditional expectations imposed by the educational system. This paper presents the findings of a study carried out from 2023 to 2024 aimed at identifying the dimensions of pedagogical success as experienced by Montessori teachers within the scope of their professional responsibilities. The study, based on a diagnostic survey conducted on a sample of 206 teachers, proved that professional success is perceived as multidimensional and processual. The key importance is attributed to a consciously created educational environment that supports the development of children's autonomy. The pedagogical success of the surveyed teachers results from their commitment to creating optimal learning conditions in accordan

title: Pluriversity as a pedagogical alternative on the example of the educational movement of the indigenous people of the Andean part of Cauca region in Colombia
abstract: The paper reveals how Misak Universidad and the Universidad Autónoma Indígena Intercultural in the Cauca region of Colombia embody the concept of pluriversity and assiociated with it emancipatory, critical, popular and indigenious pedagogies. To reveal this issue, an interpretive paradigm was employed—literature analysis combined with analysis of narrative interviews. The results of the research point to a topics previously unaddressed in Polish scholarly literature.

title: School in the Cloud – unlimited agency? The student’s experience in decentralised education as a pedagogical alternative
abstract: Amid growing debates about the need for changes in traditional education, there is a perceptible increase in interest in alternative educational models, where student agency plays a vital role. This article aims to provide a qualitative analysis of how student agency is fostered in the “School in the Cloud” environment—understood as a flexible form of education based on individualised learning processes, student autonomy, and partnership-based relationships. This study is based on in-depth interviews with thirteen students from grades VI to VIII who had attended the School in the Cloud for at least one year. The findings reveal that students perceive themselves as active agents in their learning, capable of critical reflection on the learning process, employing metacognitive strategies, and navigating the online environment with confidence while building peer relationships with fellow students in the Cloud School setting. Moreover, the results highlight a distinctive shift in teacher–student dynamics towards a more partnership-oriented approach. Concurrently, the analysis indicates certain limitations to student agency, particularly the challenges of self-directed learning and the

title: Becoming a sustainably oriented academic teacher. Self-development reflections with David Kolb’s concept in the background
abstract: Contemporary times bring us novel challenges and expectations. Deep and common teachers’ education for sustainable development (ESD) may profoundly change society’s mindsets and behaviours, but educators’ preparation, even on the academic level, is apparent, unsatisfactory, and superficial. Thus, the responsibility lies only in reflective and anticipative teachers who strive for self-development in moral and self-academic discipline education. Self-direction needs self-support. Thus, the author seeks help with theoretical concepts, research approach (autoethnography), and more practical frameworks, such as the Kolb Educator Role Profiles model. The author intends to show her path to broadening sustainable self-literacy while simultaneously looking at her activity through the lens of a self-teacher and a self-learner.

title: The theories of cultural trauma and trauma scripts – perspectives of their application in educational studies in the context of the reality of alternative matrices of knowledge and pedagogical discourses
abstract: The subject of the analysis is the application of the theories of cultural trauma and trauma scripts in educational studies. Cultural trauma is a social construct based on discourses that represent the event. They define the social identities of the participants and the scopes of responsibility and solidarity. In educational studies, the theory of cultural trauma can provide a matrix for analyzing the ways in which events are represented in hidden and overt programs, for defining the role of entities directly and indirectly related to school as representatives of carrier groups, for attributions of responsibility for the occurrence of the event, the scope of social solidarity, and commemorative practices. From such a perspective, the theory can be applied in the analysis of issues concerning school functioning and its status in civil society and structures of power competing for control over alternative structures of knowledge.

title: Glowing Riddles: On Regaining Humanity in Education
abstract: This text examines the central role of humanity in pedagogy and the interconnectedness of conceptions of humanity and education. Primarily, it analyzes the existentially degrading effects of dehumanization, focusing on the dominance of instrumental reason, the implicit agenda of the digital age, and the problematic influence of traditional humanist doctrines. Drawing on processual ontology, the text proposes an understanding of humanity in terms of question and event. This perspective leads to an interpretation of education that emphasizes the pivotal moment of pedagogical action: engaging with individual uniqueness. The argument asserts that a genuine educational concern for humanity necessitates fundamental changes in pedagogical imagination, including within humanist frameworks.

title: Between resistance and emancipation: homeschooling as an alternative educational space
abstract: The article conceptualizes parents’ decision to undertake home education as a resistance–emancipation process rather than merely an organizational alternative to schooling. Its aim is to explain the logic of this decision: from opposition to the reproductive mechanisms of schools to the creation of learning environments that safeguard the child’s identity and values. The analysis, grounded in the critical–emancipatory paradigm and the knowledge-power conflict perspective, links reflections on cultures of resistance and emancipatory pedagogy with the Polish legal and social context. The proposed heuristic model addresses the polarization of freedom-control motives, a continuum of action, motivation, space and time, the trajectory of agency in the sequence of claims-aspirations-pursuits, and the mapping of home education forms within transgressive educational cultures. The article’s contribution lies in shifting the focus from describing to explaining the phenomenon, providing an analytical language that distinguishes symbolic resistance from transformative actions, and indicating implications for educational policy, practice, and research on home education.

title: Review of Larisa Lukyanova’s Monograph “Adult education: modern strategies and practices in Ukraine and abroad”(Second edition revised and enlarged – Kiev: Talkom, 2025 – 592 pages)
abstract: REVIEW OF LARISA LUKYANOVA’S MONOGRAPHAdult education: modern strategies and practices in Ukraine and abroad(Second edition revised and enlarged – Kiev: Talkom, 2025 – 592 pages)

title: Aesthetic education and environmental activism
abstract: This essay explores environmental aesthetics as a framework for rethinking aesthetic education in general schools, highlighting its potential to foster active engagement, ethical awareness, and ecological responsibility among students. Drawing on the theories of Berleant, Saito, and others, it emphasizes a shift from object-centered to experience-oriented aesthetics. Aesthetic experience enables individuals to immerse themselves in their surroundings, integrating sensory perception, imagination, emotion, and knowledge. The essay argues that aesthetic engagement can be linked with ethical action, promoting environmentally responsible behaviors and civic participation. It also addresses the institutional and ethical challenges inherent in implementing this approach within contemporary educational contexts.

title: On reflexivity in education: alternatives and their pedagogical consequences
abstract: Reflectivity constitutes the foundation of education, being an essential element of intellectual development. The article presents four perspectives on reflectivity: pragmatic, critical, hermeneutic, and phenomenological. The pragmatic perspective, based on the ideas of Dewey and Schön, portrays reflectivity as a tool for transforming experience into knowledge and as a way of solving practical problems in education. The critical perspective, inspired by Critical Theory of the Frankfurt School and the works of Foucault and Habermas, views reflectivity as a process of exposing hidden structures of power and ideology, leading to individual emancipation. The hermeneutic perspective, rooted in interpretive traditions (Dilthey, Gadamer, van Manen), emphasizes understanding the world through language, meanings, and cultural contexts. Reflectivity here serves to interpret experience and strengthen the teacher’s self-awareness. The phenomenological perspective, grounded in the philosophy of Husserl and Arendt, focuses on introspection and the faithful description of individual experiences. Reflectivity is understood as a metacognitive act—deepening awareness of one’s own mental processes.Ea

title: Experiencing silence as one of the foundations of self-education. Review of Thich Nhat Hanh's book “Silence. The Power of Quiet in a World Full of Noise”, 2nd edition, translated by Jerzy Paweł Listwan, published by “Czarna Owca”, Warsaw 2022, pp. 178
abstract: This is a review of the book Silence by the renowned contemporary Zen master. The reviewer first presents several positions of humanities educators on the role of silence in education, which coincide with the teachings contained in the book.The reviewer also presents selected selected aspects of Thich Nhat Hanh's work, a pioneer in teaching Westerners mindfulness – Buddhist meditation. He also presents views of a Vietnamese teacher on education and his books on the subiect. Ultimately, he focuses on discussing individual chapters of the book “Silence”, referring to his own selection of the teachings contained therein and his understanding of them. The book contains elements of a life handbook and a guide to mindfulness meditation, but above all, it is a multi-layered text addressed to people at different levels of spiritual development, reflecting the essence of Buddhist teachings: co-existence, empathetic understanding or penetration of others, awakening, freedom, love and community. The teaching presented is a proposal for alternative self-education for contemporary people living in a constant rush, including pedagogues, who are encouraged to stop, subject their lives to deep ref

title: Home Education at the End of the First Quarter of the 21st Century – Still Hindered, and yet Justifiable Alternative
abstract: This article attempts to characterize the social conditions in which Polish parents and children of homeschooling have had to operate during the last five years of the post-COVID era, with necessary references to the more distant past. Regardless of their close interconnectedness, these conditions are packed into three spheres of social life: culture, economics, and politics. Home education, thus characterized, was considered here, based on the facts presented, to be a hindered, though justifiable, alternative.

title: Experiences and coping strategies of parents of adult transgender children: navigating challenges
abstract: The aim of the article is to attempt to describe the process parents go through in becoming parents of a transgender child. This process, as they define it themselves, begins with coping with difficulties and then moves on to celebrating victories. The article discusses the experiences of parents with adult transgender children in Poland, focusing on the various stages they go through. Research Method: The data were collected through narrative (biographical) interviews with parents of transgender children. The interviews were conducted among 23 parents, including 20 mothers and 3 fathers. Sampling was done using the ‘snowball effect’ method. Grounded methodology was used for data analysis. The research reveals that parents face similar difficulties and processes as parents in other countries, but with added challenges due to the lack of legal and medical support for transgender people in Poland.

title: Teachers’ Technological, Pedagogical, and Content Knowledge related to Artificial Intelligence as a Protective Factor Against Technostress and Techno-anxiety
abstract: The integration of information technology in education, including AI tools, may induce anxiety and serve as a source of significant technostress. A potential mitigating factor for both phenomena is teachers’ technological, pedagogical, and content knowledge related to AI (AI-TPACK). This hypothesis was examined in a cross-sectional, correlational study involving 364 students in teacher training programs and 55 in-service teachers. Data were collected using standardized instruments: the Abbreviated Technology Anxiety Scale (Wilson et al., 2023), the Person-Environment Fit Scale of Technostress (Wang et al., 2020), and the Intelligent Technological, Pedagogical, and Content Knowledge Scale (Celik, 2023). Results indicated low levels of techno-anxiety and technostress and moderate levels of AI-TPACK in both groups. As expected, techno-anxiety and technostress were strongly and positively correlated, while both were negatively associated with AI-TPACK. Moreover, AI-TPACK significantly moderated the relationship between techno-anxiety and technostress in selected configurations. title: Social media as a positive formative environment
abstract: The article analyzes the role of social media as a new formative environment for children and adolescents. The starting point is their growing presence in everyday life, which leads to a redefinition of socialization and upbringing processes. Particular attention is paid to the concept of digital upbringing, which transforms traditional educational relationships and opens new possibilities for parents, teachers, and institutions. The article highlights the constructive potential of social media in upbringing processes and in shaping the digital well-being of the young generation, indicating that they can serve as important support for development, socialization, and the building of social capital among children and adolescents.
